name: Inkbud
silhouette: A teardrop cuttlefish with a blunt living face, six short arm tips and two long bracket feelers; dark mantle separated from pale fins.
motion: Mantle pulses forward, fins ripple left-to-right, feelers catch up.

name: Scriptcuttle
silhouette: A long rectangular cuttlefish mantle between two scalloped fin rails; four long arms curl into open brackets beneath its large eyes.
motion: Long steady fin-wave glide, then separate left and right bracket-arm folds.

name: Fanfolio
silhouette: A broad cuttlefish with joined webbed arms spread into two offset fans; the face sits in a deep central V, with a short mantle behind.
motion: Alternating broad fan strokes, a sideways bank, and a deliberate web fold.

name: Bobclam
silhouette: A living rounded clam with two unequal chalk valves, a visible smiling hinge face and one thick scalloped foot.
motion: Foot reaches, shell tips forward, valves clap gently after the pull.

name: Keelcasket
silhouette: A long low clam with an open split-keel lower valve, broad muscular foot and an eye-bearing upper lip projecting forward.
motion: Low foot ripples while the keel rocks in opposite phase; eyelids track the path.

name: Crownfloat
silhouette: A tall clam with two thin high valves held in an open crown above its face; a short inflated foot forms a visible round ballast below.
motion: Foot inflates for a short buoyant rise then settles; valves open asymmetrically.

name: Frondfoal
silhouette: An upright seahorse with a leaf-frilled short snout, two small fins and a single hook tail with a bare visible tip.
motion: Two fin flutters, forward nod and uncoiling tail step without a static hover.

name: Trellisseer
silhouette: A tall seahorse whose paired branching back fronds frame an open ladder behind its small living face; long nearly straight tail.
motion: Long upright fin strokes; the tail straightens and the open frond ladder flexes.

name: Bowercoil
silhouette: A compact seahorse curled sideways around one broad living kelp loop, head outside the loop and fins above its low center.
motion: Tail hooks, releases and rolls one quarter-turn while the face remains upright.

name: Rimlet
silhouette: A low horseshoe-crab animal with a smooth U-shaped metal rim, two bright front eyes, six tiny feet and a slender jointed tail.
motion: Six feet scuttle in offset pairs, tail steers late and the rim dips.

name: Gateshield
silhouette: A narrow horseshoe body whose two upright rim halves form an open portal around its face; splayed rear feet and a fork-ended tail.
motion: Diagonal braced steps, opening rim halves and a two-beat gate-close gesture.

name: Stencilback
silhouette: A broad rectangular horseshoe shell with two large asymmetric open windows; a living face and short feet remain visible at its front.
motion: Wide planted stride; front shell lifts first, followed by a flat deliberate stamp.

name: Ventplume
silhouette: A short soft tube-worm with a rounded face below a forked warm feather crown; flexible pale tube ends in three root toes.
motion: Toes grip, tube stretches, crown opens and contracts in a breathing beat.

name: Haloworm
silhouette: A tall tube-worm whose two offset half-fan crowns leave an open crescent above its blinking face; a narrow coiled foot.
motion: Foot uncoils, neck bows, two half-fans open in opposite order.

name: Trailwick
silhouette: A low long tube-worm with four separated glowing mantle folds, exposed forward eyes and a single trailing wick-like feeler.
motion: Muscular waves travel along the soft tube; folds brighten from head to tail.

name: Palmstar
silhouette: A soft five-armed sea star with a raised expressive center and broad kelp-edged arm tips; gaps are wide and individually readable.
motion: Two arms plant while three reach; the raised face tilts before each turn.

name: Crossbloom
silhouette: A high-centered star with four long unequal cross arms and a fifth short rear arm; open diagonal gaps and a face held above the center.
motion: Opposite arms extend together and the center rises, then alternating arms settle.

name: Foldrunner
silhouette: A long folded star animal walking on three joined zigzag arms while two short forearms frame its face; no radial silhouette at rest.
motion: A traveling accordion fold changes the two major bends; forearms feel the next step.

name: Linkeel
silhouette: A slender eel with a soft blunt face, three separated metallic collar plates and a flexible bare tail; no legs or wing fins.
motion: One lateral body wave travels through all three loose collars; eyes lead the turn.

name: Hingejaw
silhouette: An angular eel with two long articulated body sections, an open elbow gap and a broad hinged jaw around a visible living face.
motion: Front segment aims, rear segment swings around a clearly planted joint, jaw closes.

name: Claspcoil
silhouette: A short thick eel curled into an unequal figure eight with two open loops; face rests beside the crossing and tail remains free.
motion: Large loop contracts as small loop expands, then the crossing moves one foot-length.

name: Combgleam
silhouette: A translucent oval comb-jelly with a small face, four broad ciliary comb bands and two short joined feeding lobes, never an umbrella.
motion: Four comb bands ripple in sequence while the oval body compresses lengthwise.

name: Veilglass
silhouette: A tall diamond comb-jelly with one broad diagonal veil and two separated trailing lobes; its face shows through a pale central window.
motion: Diagonal veil folds across the body and opens on the other side; lobes trail.

name: Triadome
silhouette: A low triangular comb-jelly with three connected soft corner lobes around an open-looking central window; two eyes sit on the leading lobe.
motion: Three corners pulse one at a time, giving a slow turning glide and clear landing shadow.
